title: Aletheia — risk and latency
description: The panels are ordered by what would make you intervene. Answer rate and uncalibrated abstentions come first because they are product failures that no error rate would reveal: the system is up, fast, and returning nothing useful.

panels.title: Answer rate
panels.description: Fraction of requests that returned an answer rather than abstaining. PRD G2 targets >= 70% at alpha=0.05. A healthy-looking system with a collapsed answer rate is the characteristic failure of this design — every probe is green and users get nothing.

panels.title: Abstentions we caused
panels.description: stale_calibration means no certified, fresh threshold was available — the system declining because of us, not because the corpus lacked an answer. Should be zero. A non-zero value means the calibration job has stopped running or its output has aged out.

panels.title: Decisions
panels.description: answer / answer_with_flags / abstain over time. A shift towards abstain without a deploy usually means the corpus changed under a threshold fitted to the old one.

panels.title: Why we abstained
panels.description: insufficient_evidence and out_of_corpus are the corpus talking. stale_calibration and any spike correlated with a deploy are us.

panels.title: Degraded responses
panels.description: Responses where the guarantee could not be established as stated. These are correct behaviour, not errors — but a rising line means a dependency is failing and the product is quietly getting less useful.

panels.title: End-to-end latency (p50 / p95)
panels.description: PRD 4.2: p50 <= 1.8s, p95 <= 3.5s including the verifier. Measured at 84ms / 182ms with the overlap verifier; the NLI verifier costs seconds per response and is the open problem (eval/results/week8-latency.md).

panels.title: p95 by stage
panels.description: Which stage owns the tail. Retrieval and the verifier are the two that move; the verifier is expected to dominate once NLI is enabled.

panels.title: Throttled requests
panels.description: Rate limiting and the concurrency cap are reported separately because they need different client-side fixes. Sustained throttling of one tenant is working as intended; throttling across all tenants means the limits are too tight for real traffic.

panels.title: Ingestion outcomes
panels.description: created / amended / corrected / unchanged. A sync that reports mostly 'unchanged' is healthy — it means content hashing is doing its job and no false corpus drift is being manufactured. A burst of 'amended' invalidates the exchangeability assumption the guarantee rests on.

panels.title: Retrieval results per arm
panels.description: Lexical and dense fail in uncorrelated ways (ADR-0006). An arm flatlining at zero while the other keeps working is the failure mode hybrid retrieval exists to survive — and the one no error rate would show.
